title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
Cursor Agent, an AI coding and task assistant running Claude Sonnet, was used by Aurora ransomware operators as an active exploitation tool inside compromised networks. The operators directed it to perform network scanning, privilege enumeration, and NTLM relay attacks, tasks that fall well outside the conditions the tool was built for. This is a case of an AI assistant being weaponised by attackers who already had a foothold, not a failure of the AI system's own deployment pipeline. The tool did not malfunction, it was used as intended by its operators, but those operators were malicious actors rather than legitimate users.

The failure mode here is the absence of effective guardrails or usage controls that would prevent an authenticated session of the tool from being directed at third-party systems without authorisation. Nothing in the reported facts indicates Cursor Agent detected or refused the hostile tasks. Detection came from outside, through threat intelligence researchers examining attacker behaviour after the fact, not from any safety mechanism within the tool itself.

What is not established is whether the operators circumvented any specific safety controls, what volume of harm resulted from the AI-assisted intrusions versus the non-AI cluster's activity, and the full scope of victim organisations, the reporting identifies ten organisations for the AI-using cluster but the final count and attribution remain part of an ongoing investigation rather than a concluded finding.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
Gambit Security's threat intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual environments. The group uses a sophisticated encryptor that kills running virtual machines to unlock files, then encrypts VM data while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands. Between April and May 2026, Aurora operators deployed Cursor Agent, an AI assistant running Claude Sonnet, across ten victim organizations to conduct hands-on exploitation tasks including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and NTLM relay attacks.

A second Aurora cluster was identified using different tactics, affecting eight organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, and the United States. This group exfiltrated data via S3 storage and used SQL Server vulnerabilities and DCSync attacks instead of AI tools. Researchers provided detailed technical indicators, including command-line options for the ransomware, infrastructure IP addresses, and the group's onion site for ransom negotiations, enabling organizations to strengthen their defenses against these threats.
